handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

session_context.purpose: Resume Phase 1 pipeline tuning for Killdeer Meadows. Two tasks: (1) review the system prompt in m3_infer.py for any additional co-occurrence rules to add, then (2) run test 7.
session_context.first_thing_next_session: Read phase1/inference/m3_infer.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (approx lines 200–600) and cross-reference the item_pairs in the holdout knowledge pack at phase1/knowledge_pack/holdout_25016-2_kildere_meadows/knowledge_pack.json. Look for: (a) high-co_occurrence pairs (>=0.75) not yet handled by the current Item Pairs rule, and (b) any remaining hardcoded item rules that could be replaced with statistical co-occurrence guidance. Then run test 7 per the commands below.

test_7_commands.note: Never run Python scripts directly. Tell Nolan the command and wait for him to paste output back.

session_context.after_test_7: Compare line-by-line against actual Killdeer Meadows proposal. Actuals are in phase1/case_library/25055-1_KILLDEER_MEADOWS.json. Pay special attention to: 6" SIDEWALKS (was missing in test 6), 1" IRR SERVICE (was 18 EA in test 6, actual is 2 EA), DEMOLITION (was missing in test 6), EXC TO EMBANK (was undercounted in test 6), and road_LF accuracy (new 5-priority Gemini prompt was updated this session).

test_5.verdict: First Killdeer test. Major overcount on 1" IRR SERVICE (18 EA vs actual 2 EA). Missing DEMOLITION. road_LF over-extracted by Gemini.

test_6.verdict: Improved. Remaining gap: IRR SERVICE still overcounted (18 vs 2), DEMO still missing, 6" SIDEWALKS missing, EXC TO EMBANK underestimated. Opposing errors partially cancel.

gemini_road_LF_prompt.what: Replaced the original profile-first road_LF extraction with a 5-source priority order
gemini_road_LF_prompt.why: Gemini was summing all profiled road segments including existing roads, yielding ~1,700 LF vs ~1,309 LF. The new priority puts explicit title/callout labels first, profile view last, and adds caution about PVI/BVC/EVC annotations being mistaken for construction limits.
new_priority_order: 1. ROAD NAME + STATIONING on title/prominent label — e.g. 'KILLDEER AVE STA:10+50 TO STA:21+00'
2. EXPLICIT LF CALLOUT — e.g. 'L=979.62\'' or 'TOTAL LENGTH = 475 LF'
3. BEGIN/END CONSTRUCTION text paired with station numbers
4. PLAN VIEW station tick marks along centerline
5. PROFILE VIEW x-axis — proposed (solid) portion only; ignore PVI/BVC/EVC annotations
gemini_road_LF_prompt.road_LF_segments_schema: road_LF_segments field added to Gemini JSON schema: [{road_name, lf_source, start_sta, end_sta, proposed_LF}] for auditability
gemini_road_LF_prompt.gemini_extraction_sidecar: gemini_extract() now writes a .gemini_extraction.md sidecar file showing all extracted scale metrics plus each road segment's LF, source, and station range

system_prompt_changes.curb_type: Removed 'mutually exclusive' language. C&G and rolled curb can coexist on the same job (e.g. C&G at intersections, rolled curb on residential streets). Killdeer had both.
system_prompt_changes.irrigation_services: NEW: 1" IRR SERVICE is a district connection at the road right-of-way, never per-lot. Max 1–3 EA total; default to road_connection_count. This was the source of the +18 EA overcount.
system_prompt_changes.demolition: NEW: always include a DEMOLITION line item if scope_notes mentions demolition. Was missing entirely in tests 5 and 6.

item_pairs_rule.what: Replaced the hardcoded 6" SIDEWALKS rule with a statistical co-occurrence rule
item_pairs_rule.rule: When computing any line item, scan item_pairs for a partner where co_occurrence_rate >= 0.75. If partner is not already in estimate and not excluded by 2+ closest analogs, include it. Derive partner_qty using median_ratio_a_to_b.
item_pairs_rule.why: Self-updating as case library grows. 4" SIDEWALKS ↔ 6" SIDEWALKS pair has r=0.975, co_occurrence_rate=0.80 — will trigger auto-include of 6" when 4" is computed.

system_prompt_changes.exc_to_embank: NEW: floor $20,000, flag [EST], removed no-borrow assumption. Was being underestimated.
system_prompt_changes.signs_and_striping: Removed from auto-exclude list. Check analogs first — some jobs genuinely include it.

derive_patterns_py.filters: EA, LF, SF, SY units only; |r| >= 0.85; N >= 4 shared jobs
derive_patterns_py.output_per_pair: item_a, item_b, unit_a, unit_b, r, n_shared_jobs, n_jobs_a, n_jobs_b, co_occurrence_rate, median_ratio_a_to_b, shared_jobs

eda_notebook.cell_15: Filter changed from {EA, LF} to {EA, LF, SF, SY}. Variable ea_lf → all_meas. Heatmap title updated.
